summary: Root cause: scene_off_flashlight_on was grouped into its own scene-off render instance, but the scene-off path only hid existing light components and the RGB capture path still used Lumen/reflection/temporal capture settings from the BP camera sensor. That could leave brightness/history effects that visually resembled scene-on lighting and could flicker. I made scene-off disabling zero direct and indirect light intensity in addition to visibility, and made default orbit renders deterministic when render history is disabled.
work_completed: Updated scene-off light disabling in examples/flashlight/run_orbit_collection.py to hide every existing ULightComponentBase and zero both SetIntensity and SetIndirectLightingIntensity where supported before render frames are captured.

Added deterministic orbit render config for default render-history-disabled captures: disables anti-aliasing/Temporal AA, motion blur, Lumen GI, Lumen reflections, reflection method, and screen-space reflections in the render instance engine INI.

Added capture-component hardening for deterministic renders: bAlwaysPersistRenderingState is disabled and DynamicGlobalIllumination/Reflection post-process overrides are cleared so the BP camera sensor cannot force Lumen back on for explicit captures.
Added per-setting metadata.json output recording scene_lights_enabled, scene-light disable/scale counts, auto-exposure/render-history state, and deterministic capture component state.
Added focused tests for scene-light zeroing, deterministic capture component configuration, metadata output, and deterministic render config preservation/opt-out behavior.
Updated orbit workflow docs to describe deterministic render-history-disabled behavior and metadata output.

findings.message: scene_lights_enabled=false did reach a separate render group and set disable_scene_lights, but the previous implementation only called SetVisibility(false); it did not force light intensity/indirect intensity to zero, and it did not address scene capture Lumen/reflection/temporal state.
Default render collection now favors deterministic data capture over fancy temporal rendering. --enable-render-history remains the opt-in path for normal temporal renderer comparison.

Full pytest/unittest execution could not run in this environment because pytest and numpy are not installed. Static py_compile passed, and a targeted smoke check of the new pure-Python light disable, capture configuration, and metadata helpers passed.

follow_up_recommendations: Live validation command for the user: examples/flashlight/run_orbit_workflow.sh render --output-dir examples/flashlight/orbit_collection_output_validation

Inspect examples/flashlight/orbit_collection_output_validation/scene_off_flashlight_on/metadata.json after the run; scene_lights_enabled should be false, direct_intensity_zeroed should match the discovered light component count where SetIntensity is supported, and deterministic capture states should be true for the RGB/depth capture components.
memory_worthy: For flashlight orbit collection, default render-history-disabled renders should disable temporal/Lumen capture paths and scene-off should zero light intensities, not only hide components.
